subject: Proration request — sync gap between BrightBridge connector and Redwood usage
messages:
From: Alexa Moreno <alexa@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: BrightBridge Procurement <procurement@brightbridgehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy in July usage — possible duplicate ingestion

Hi Karthik,

Our finance team flagged a ~22% variance between the usage totals shown on the Redwood invoice (Invoice 2026-07) and the export we pull from our ingestion connector. The difference starts on July 12 and spikes July 20–24. I've attached our billing_export_july.csv and the invoice for reference.

From a quick look the duplicate rows seem correlated with when our connector re-tried failed uploads (we had a short outage in our ETL). Can Redwood confirm whether retries are de-duplicated at ingestion or if they count as additional tokens?

This is blocking our month-end close — can we get a short investigation and, if appropriate, a prorated credit while you reconcile?

Thanks,
Alexa Moreno
Head of Finance Ops
BrightBridge Health

Attachments: billing_export_july.csv (csv), invoice_2026-07.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Alexa Moreno <alexa@brightbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in July usage — possible duplicate ingestion

Hi Alexa — thanks for the files, and sorry to hear this is impacting close. Quick answers up front:
- Redwood de-duplicates requests at the request-id level when present; if your connector retried with different request ids each attempt those retries will count as additional consumption.
- We can run a token-level sample and compare request ids/timestamps for the July 12–24 window.

Can you attach a small sample of the connector logs showing the retry behavior (timestamps + request ids) and the CSV column mapping you’re using? I attached a connector-log-sample.txt that shows what we need. If you prefer, Marissa (CS) can open a support ticket and we can add a temporary invoice hold while we investigate.

I’ll triage on our side and ask infra to run a per-route usage diff for that period.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: connector-log-sample.txt

From: Alexa Moreno <alexa@brightbridgehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: BrightBridge Procurement <procurement@brightbridgehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in July usage — possible duplicate ingestion

Thanks Karthik — attaching the small slice you requested (usage-export-2026-07.csv). You’ll see the retry sequence in rows 1127–1140: same payload id but different request_id values and repeated token counts. We haven't been intentionally changing request ids — it's the connector retry logic.

Finance is requesting a provisional credit for the duplicated tokens while Redwood completes reconciliation. If you can provide a hold or statement we can include in our ledger, that would help.

Also, can you confirm whether de-duplication behavior differs between Hosted and Dedicated modes? We are on Hosted.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Alexa

Attachments: usage-export-2026-07.csv

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
To: Alexa Moreno <alexa@brightbridgehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 08:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in July usage — possible duplicate ingestion

Hi Alexa — Neha from Finance here. Could you also share the invoice line-item that maps to the ingestion route (route id or name) and the accounting code you use? On our side, we'll: 
1) Create a provisional credit memo for the duplicated tokens for July 12–24 (pending final reconciliation).
2) Ask Infra to run a token-level reconciliation and provide a CSV with matched request_id pairs and delta.

Regarding Hosted vs Dedicated: behavior is consistent — de-duplication only happens when the request includes the same client-provided request_id. Automatic retries that generate new IDs will be counted as new consumption on all deployment modes. If you need retries to be ignored, we can advise on connector-level idempotency headers or add a middleware dedupe for you in Hosted as a limited exception.

I'll approve a provisional credit up to the delta flagged in your sample; final credit amount will materialize after the infra run. Expect an initial credit memo emailed to procurement by Monday.

Neha Kapoor
Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.example>
To: Alexa Moreno <alexa@brightbridgehealth.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in July usage — possible duplicate ingestion

Alexa — quick update to close the loop for your finance team: 
- Infra ran the token-level comparison and found 3,482 duplicated requests between July 12–24 matching your retry pattern.
- Neha approved a provisional credit for 3,482 * effective token unit price as a one-line credit memo applied to Invoice 2026-07. The provisional memo id is CM-BBH-0826-01 and will appear in HubSpot (link below).
- Short-term mitigation: we enabled an opt-in hosted dedupe middleware for your account that will ignore retries if the payload hash and client_request_id match; this will be active until your engineering team deploys a connector fix.

Marissa will send the credit memo pdf and the reconciliation CSV (matched_request_ids.csv) to procurement; procurement can apply the credit during their ledger close. If anything else pops up, I’m here.

Thanks for the quick collaboration — I'll follow up once the final credit posts.

—Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Related HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/company/987654321/engagements/5555555
Attachments referenced: matched_request_ids.csv, CM-BBH-0826-01.pdf
